text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert - spike in 5xx/timeouts on api-gateway (region-us). p95 jumped from 220ms -> 6.8s, p99 570ms -> 18.2s over the last 3m. Error budget burn triggered. Detector: deploy-diff. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/in/c/abc123
arjun: saw it. just rolled out runtime-proxy 2026-03-15T09:02 (canary 10%). can confirm requests to /v1/generate are timing out with upstream 504s.
maria: canary-only or global? grafana shows canary hosts high error rate, stable hosts low. looks canary-localized so far.
ryan: pinging oncall, tagging @sre-oncall. canary is 10% traffic, but backend KV cache is also showing increased miss latency around same time.
priya: checking logs, fast failure pattern from runtime-proxy to backend: "upstream timeout after 10s". stack shows heavy queue length on proxy workers.
arjun: rolling canary back to previous revision now. running: ```kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/runtime-proxy --to-revision=42```
ops-bot: Rollout undo initiated for runtime-proxy -> rev 42. Watch pods terminating and new ones becoming ready.
console-bot: Route shift requested: set traffic-api -> stable (kick canary to 0%). Command: `rdrctl traffic shift api-gateway --set-canary 0`
maria: starting synthetic curl checks against /health and a small generation call: ```for i in {1..5}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood/v1/generate; done``` outputs: many 504 10.01s then after rollback some 200 0.12s
arjun: rollback completed on canary pods, new pods at rev42 are ready. still watching p95/p99.
ryan: alerting product/CS: potential customer impact on real-time generative endpoints, reaching out to top-10 customers for heads-up. @customer-success fyi.
customer-success: acknowledged. prepping brief statement; will hold until metrics stable.
priya: digging into root cause hypothesis: kernel-level epoll backlog bump + a change in runtime-proxy connection pool sizing (the canary enabled aggressive multiplexing). reproducing locally with load test.
arjun: quick mitigation checklist we did: 1) rollback canary 2) shift traffic to stable 3) scale api-gateway frontends by +20% 4) disable multiplexing flag on hot path 5) monitor.
ops-bot: HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaled api-gateway from 8 -> 10 replicas.
maria: p95 dropped back to ~240ms within 90s of rollback. p99 trending down from 18s -> 600ms -> 220ms over 7m.
ryan: confirm no customer-facing rate limit events. logs show an initial tranche of failed requests but no long tail customer errors after rollback.
arjun: keeping thread open for handoff. leaving a note for postmortem. adding tracer snapshots to incident ticket INC-2026-033.
on-urgent: code snippet of offending flag in runtime-proxy config: ```runtime_proxy:
  multiplexing: true   # introduced 2026-03-15
  conn_pool_max: 1024
  worker_threads: 12
```
priya: preliminary root cause: multiplexing change + insufficient backpressure on conn_pool -> queuing -> timeouts at tail. will validate with repro and a perf patch.
on-urgent: recommend warm-fix: revert multiplexing flag immediately on candidate branch then run controlled canary with increased sampling and KV warmup.
on-urgent: followups assigned: arjun (deploy revert PR), priya (perf repro + tests), maria (post-deploy canary gating), ryan (customer comms).
on-urgent: oncall-next: @oncall-next pls take watch for the next 2 hours and escalate if p99 > 1s for more than 5m.
on-urgent: oncall-next: acknowledged, will monitor.
incident-bot: Incident resolved state: mitigation applied (canary rollback), p95/p99 back within SLOs. Incident duration ~ 16m. Ticket: INC-2026-033.
arjun: adding a short runbook note for this pattern: "voter-fallback" - when a canary enables multiplexing that increases head-of-line latency, perform immediate canary rollback + traffic shift and scale frontends.
priya: will submit PR to disable multiplexing by default and add circuit breaker for conn_pool.
maria: recording for postmortem: timeline, dashboards, rollback commands, reproducible load test.
ryan: thanks all. closing active pager. handing to oncall-next for 2h watch.,
oncall-next: oncall-next here, watching metrics and alerts. will open PM if regressions reappear.
customer-success: closing internal comms thread after ops confirms no sustained customer errors.
incident-bot: This thread will be archived in 7 days. Remember to attach eval prompts and canary gating checks to the postmortem.
